comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Dutch-route regulations, annual plan pp. 22–23, determine the 60 EC per year ledger and neutral choice order. The study guide lists Maghreb before Latin America in its second-period menu. Both are eligible, and this illustration follows the adopted annual plan order consistently. Year three starts with 30 EC of profiling space, then requires Culture, Religion and Knowledge and one global research seminar, colloquium and thesis. Regulations arts. 9.1 and 12.1–12.2 control progression and elective rules. The Dutch test is 0 EC. The current late-medieval and early-modern seminar uses Low Countries manuscripts and early print for lay devotion. The chosen global seminar uses photography in modern politics. Topics can change.
components: Origins of History: The Globalizing Mediterranean World, 3500 BCE–1000 CE
Students must complete the Dutch language test or required remedial work before the course grade is recorded.
One of the approved choices in period 1.

Research Seminar in Culture, Religion and Knowledge, 500–1800
The current seminar studies lay devotion in the Low Countries through manuscripts and early printed works.
Research Seminar in Global and Political History, 1500 to the Present
The selected seminar examines political history through photography. Students take one of the two global research seminars.
Students need an agreed thesis topic and supervisor and a signed thesis agreement by the start of period 4.
An individually supervised study of historical literature that may also use primary sources. The thesis grade requires successful completion of the colloquium.
Students may choose a minor, elective courses, study abroad or a 12 EC internship plus 18 EC of courses. Individually chosen courses must include at least 12 EC at level 300. Approval rules apply.

routeSelection.basis: Broadest Dutch-taught route. Illustrative electives and the extra research seminar follow the order in the adopted annual plan.

alternatives.label: History, cultural heritage & public memory
alternatives.concept: Study modern history, gender, empire, warfare and Indigenous histories, then use archaeology, art, life writing and media to explore how people interpret and remember the past. The final history seminar develops a research paper on American history.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the sustained 45 EC dedicated History core and the actual distinct companion disciplines; no specialised migration/economic-history or full external-degree claim.
progression: Six terms with 24 courses. Historical study leads into the advanced research seminar. Current offerings and workbook prerequisites are satisfied.

alternatives.label: History, political conflict & social inclusion
alternatives.concept: Study empire, warfare, gender and Indigenous histories alongside political institutions, rights, peace and conflict, and social inclusion. Contemporary politics and sociology provide additional ways to investigate power and exclusion. The final history seminar develops a research paper on American history.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the sustained 45 EC dedicated History core and the actual distinct companion disciplines; no specialised migration/economic-history or full external-degree claim.
progression: Six terms with 24 courses. Historical study leads into the advanced research seminar. Current offerings and workbook prerequisites are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: The organising choice materially changes course selection: political theory, institutions, rights, peace/conflict and migrant inclusion replace the extensive art, museum and media-history sequence.

alternatives.label: History, political economy & global inequality
alternatives.concept: Study modern history and empire alongside economics, statistics, social theory and European institutions. These tools help explain economic change and inequality. The final history seminar develops a research paper on American history.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the sustained 45 EC dedicated History core and the actual distinct companion disciplines; no specialised migration/economic-history or full external-degree claim.
progression: Six terms with 24 courses. Historical study leads into the advanced research seminar. Current offerings and workbook prerequisites are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: Five economics courses, including Econometrics and Public Economics, build the political economy direction alongside comparative institutional and social inquiry.

selection.assessment: Each option retains the six-course historical core, including modern history, gender and interviews, empire, warfare, Indigenous histories and a sustained research paper on American history. The first option builds cultural and public-memory interpretation through art, archaeology, narrative and media. The second develops political institutions, rights, conflict and social inclusion. The third builds economic explanation and inference alongside institutional and social inquiry. No separate crime or migration-history sequence is supported. VU retains period and regional depth and specialist historical methods beyond these UCR options.

blocks: Both examine modern European change. UCR begins in the nineteenth century and also follows developments beyond Europe.
Both use interviews to investigate the past. UCR applies them to North American gender histories, while VU also teaches preparation of interviews for digital archives.
Both examine historical changes across world regions. UCR focuses on empires, and VU surveys world history more broadly.
Both develop historical research questions and use sources to build an argument. UCR’s seminar focuses on American history, while VU’s seminar studies early modern knowledge in the Netherlands.
UCR studies ancient societies through material evidence. VU follows the changing Mediterranean world across a much longer period.
Both address early modern European culture. UCR focuses on Renaissance Italian art and exchange, while VU covers a wider period and range of historical changes.
External specialist depth, research and academic profile
VU teaches academic research skills specifically for historians.
VU gives historical writing its own course.
VU develops historical explanations of current events for a broad audience.
VU gives religion and state formation a dedicated historical course.
VU studies environmental questions through historical cases.
VU examines democratic revolutions as historical events.
VU requires dedicated study of the Holocaust and genocide.
VU analyses personal accounts, oral histories and oral traditions in global and colonial history.
VU teaches digital tools for historical research.
This VU choice examines the history of modern Latin America.
The current seminar studies lay devotion in the Low Countries through manuscripts and early printed works.
VU requires a colloquium with interim presentations and discussion of the thesis.
VU requires a 9 EC individual thesis. UCR’s optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.
VU sets aside 30 EC for elective study.
UCR introduces Western philosophy. VU organizes this course around selected philosophical texts.
VU examines capitalism and inequality as historical developments. UCR economics courses teach related concepts such as redistribution and public spending.
UCR teaches general statistical inference. VU works with historical numerical sources and uses tools such as pivot tables, visualizations and maps.
VU develops specialist methods for interpreting photography and photographic archives in political history.

notes.text: VU includes specialist study of the Netherlands, medieval and early modern Europe, the Holocaust and genocide, and digital history. It also requires an individual thesis. The UCR options share a history research seminar on American history and add different cultural, political or economic perspectives.

audience.programmeDescription: VU History studies Europe and the wider world from antiquity to the present. Students learn to evaluate historical evidence, develop arguments and conduct research through source-based seminars and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: All three UCR options build on six history courses and finish with a history research seminar. Choose among cultural heritage and public memory, political conflict and social inclusion, or political economy and global inequality. VU includes more specialist historical coursework and requires an individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC example includes one elective in each of the first two periods of year two. In year three, students complete 30 EC of elective study, two research seminars, a colloquium and a thesis. Both seminars require completion of year one. The thesis and colloquium require completion of years one and two. Research topics and offerings can change.
